record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: For Stable Marriage instances with uncertain preferences in the compact-indifference model, determine the computational complexity of SM Probability: given a matching, compute the probability that it is stable when each agent's weak order is refined uniformly at random to a strict preference order.

evidence.quote: 1. PO / SM Probability: What is the probability that a given matching is Pareto optimal / stable?
Question marks denote the open cases.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Stable Marriage problem with uncertain preferences in the compact-indifference model. An instance consists of two disjoint sets of agents (e.g. "men" and "women") of equal size, and for each agent a weak order (a total preorder with possible ties) over the agents of the opposite side. A strict preference profile is obtained by independently refining each agent's weak order into a strict linear order uniformly at random among all linear extensions of that weak order. A perfect matching M between the two sides is stable with respect to a strict profile if there is no blocking pair, i.e. no pair (m, w) with m and w not matched to each other in M such that m strictly prefers w to his partner in M and w strictly prefers m to her partner in M.

SM Probability: given an instance in the compact-indifference model together with a perfect matching M, compute the probability that M is stable when the random strict profile is drawn as above.

Determine the exact computational complexity of SM Probability in this model (in particular, decide whether it is solvable in polynomial time or #P-hard).
artifact.status_search_result: The complexity of computing the stability probability of a given matching in the compact-indifference model is reported in the literature on stable matching with uncertain linear preferences as still unresolved: it is known that deciding whether the stability probability is nonzero is in P (it reduces to weak stability in SMTI), but neither a polynomial-time algorithm nor a #P-hardness proof for the actual probability computation has been established. No subsequent work appears to have closed this gap.

status_evidence.snippet: Three models of uncertainty including the compact indifference model are studied; the complexity of computing the probability that a given matching is stable in the compact-indifference model is left open.
